papers.title: The universe is slowing down. Obviously. Right?
papers.hook: Two rival teams raced to measure how fast the universe is slowing. The answer looked so wrong they spent months trying to kill it.
papers.citation: Riess et al. 1998 · The Astronomical Journal

papers.title: The AI memorized everything… then suddenly understood.
papers.hook: Networks trained far past the point of memorization abruptly snap into real understanding — long after training should have stopped.

papers.title: The neural net that found two planets.
papers.hook: Google and NASA pointed a network at old telescope data. It caught worlds that human astronomers had missed.

papers.title: The planet that shouldn't exist.
papers.hook: The first planet found around another sun was a Jupiter hugging its star — impossible, according to every formation theory.

papers.title: Grandmasters don't have better memory than you.
papers.hook: Show a master a real chess position for 5 seconds and they recall it almost perfectly. Scramble the pieces randomly, and their superpower vanishes.

papers.title: Part of your cells used to be an invader.
papers.hook: Mitochondria have their own DNA — because two billion years ago, they were free-living bacteria that got swallowed and never left.

papers.title: The fake surgery worked just as well.
papers.hook: Patients got knee surgery — or a sham operation with only skin incisions. Two years later, both groups reported the same relief.
papers.citation: Moseley et al. 2002 · New England Journal of Medicine

papers.title: The idea that got her demoted won the Nobel Prize.
papers.hook: Katalin Karikó spent decades being told mRNA therapy was a dead end. Then it vaccinated the planet.
